claims.text: The target material is a crystalline, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticle composed of five or more metals.
The proposed intervention is incorporation of oxygen or carbon into the nanoparticle composition.
Introducing oxygen or carbon could overcome instability during catalytic operation at 773–1173 K.
Introducing oxygen or carbon could enhance solid-solution strengthening.
Enhanced solid-solution strengthening would improve nanoparticle thermal stability.
Introducing oxygen or carbon would improve catalytic performance relative to untreated nanoparticles.
Introducing oxygen or carbon would improve nanoparticle stability relative to untreated nanoparticles in the 773–1173 K regime.
The proposed mechanism is supported by partially transferable insights from appraised evidence records.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requests and describes a single intervention, but the intervention is left as two materially distinct alternatives—oxygen or carbon—without selecting one.
The mechanism says it is supported by appraised evidence records, but no supporting evidence records are cited.
